decisions.reason: The article requires a regulator-and-motor assembly and may require a door module, while the unscoped claim is only a window motor and has no confirmed catalog application.

sourceEvidence.title: Window Regulator and Motor Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace window motor and regulator assembly. TSB #08-011-07 REV. A addresses front window issues requiring door module replacement. Check fuse first. Verify window switches functioning before replacing regulator.

decisions.reason: PCV replacement is only one conditional step after sludge and oil-pressure diagnosis, and the unscoped PC272 claim was not confirmed by the catalog.

sourceEvidence.title: 3.5L V6 Engine Oil Sludge and Consumption
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Start by verifying oil consumption and sludge severity: inspect under the oil fill cap/valve covers, check hot idle oil pressure with a mechanical gauge, listen for valvetrain noise, and perform a compression/leak-down test to rule out worn rings or valve seals. If sludge is moderate, remove the valve covers and oil pan to manually clean sludge, clear the cylinder head drain-back passages, replace the PCV valve, and refill with the correct viscosity full-synthetic oil plus a quality filter; if oil pressure is low, inspect/replace the oil pump pickup tube and screen, and repair bearing damage as needed. Engines with persistent consumption may also need valve stem seals or internal engine work, while severe sludge may justify replacing the engine rather than attempting repeated flushes, which can dislodge debris and worsen oil starvation. Typical costs range from about $300-$700 for inspection, cleaning, PCV service, and fresh oil, $800-$1,800 if oil pan/valve cover removal and pickup cleaning are required, and $2,500-$5,000+ for major internal repair or engine replacement.

decisions.reason: The power-steering-pump claim lacks engine/application scope and the catalog did not confirm Cardone 21-5410 for the frozen article.

sourceEvidence.title: Power Steering Pump Whine and Leak
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace power steering pump and flush the system with fresh ATF+4 (Chrysler uses ATF as power steering fluid). Check all hoses and the rack and pinion for leaks. Use only Mopar-approved fluid.

decisions.reason: The compressor is a prescribed repair, but the unscoped Denso 471-1293 claim was not confirmed for the frozen Crossfire application.

sourceEvidence.title: A/C Compressor Failure and Interior Deterioration
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace A/C compressor. Source interior trim clips and parts from Mercedes SLK R170 donor vehicles. Headlight lenses can be resealed. Junkyard Mercedes SLK R170s are excellent parts sources since wheelbase and track width are identical to SLK320.

decisions.reason: The article spans multiple 2.2L, 2.5L, and 3.0L applications, while the unscoped Delphi TS10019 claim was not confirmed for any reviewed slice.

sourceEvidence.title: Coolant Temperature Sensor Failure — Hot Stall, Erratic Gauge, Hard Restart
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Test the ECT sensor's resistance cold and hot against spec and inspect/repair the connector for corrosion; replace the sensor if out of range (Mopar coolant temperature sensor for the 2.2/2.5/3.0). Verify the cooling fan commands on and the gauge tracks after replacement. Rule out air in the cooling system and a stuck thermostat, which mimic an erratic gauge.

sourceEvidence.title: Power Window Motor Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace window motor. Check the wiring harness in the door jamb for broken wires where it flexes. Clean or replace corroded connectors. The master window switch should also be tested as a potential cause.

decisions.reason: The article requires TPMS sensor replacement and programming; a Bosch vehicle battery is the wrong repair role.

sourceEvidence.title: TPMS Sensor Battery Failure and False Warnings
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the failed TPMS sensor(s). TPMS sensors cannot be battery-replaced — the entire sensor unit must be swapped. OEM sensors (Mopar 68399563AA) cost $40-$60 each and must be programmed to the vehicle using a TPMS relearn tool or dealer scan tool. Aftermarket programmable sensors from Autel or ATEQ are available for less ($20-$35 each). Replace all four sensors simultaneously if the vehicle is 5+ years old to avoid return visits.

decisions.reason: The valve-cover gasket is diagnosis-dependent and the unscoped MAHLE VS50248 claim was not confirmed by the catalog for the frozen Prowler application.

sourceEvidence.title: 3.5L Cam/Crank Sensor O-ring & Valve Cover Oil Weeping
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Clean and pinpoint the source (cam sensor O-ring vs valve cover gasket vs cam bearing cap). Replace the hardened cam position sensor O-ring and/or valve cover gaskets with updated seals; clean the sensor connector so oil cannot re-wick into it. Address the leak before it contaminates the cam sensor or ignition components.

decisions.reason: The condenser is directly prescribed, but the unscoped Denso 477-0817 claim was not confirmed by the current all-year catalog run.

sourceEvidence.title: A/C Condenser Leak from Road Debris Impact
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the A/C condenser. The condenser is accessible from the front of the vehicle after removing the front bumper cover and grille. Replace the receiver/drier at the same time (standard practice) and install a new expansion valve if the system has been open to atmosphere for an extended period. Evacuate and recharge with the correct amount of R-134a. Budget $400-$700 for parts and labor. Consider installing a small mesh screen behind the grille to protect the new condenser.

decisions.reason: Radiator-cap replacement is one branch of a multi-cause overheating diagnosis, and Gates 31518 was not catalog-confirmed for the frozen vehicle scope.

sourceEvidence.title: Chronic Overheating - Multiple Causes
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Diagnose root cause systematically: check fan relay (5149541AA) first, then fan motor, thermostat (Stant 45359), water pump, and radiator. Replace radiator cap (frequently causes overpressure issues). Cooling fan module 5017407AB for complete fan assembly replacement.

decisions.component: Engine Timing Belt Kit with Water Pump
decisions.reason: The article specifies generation-specific Gates complete kits, while Continental CK265LK2 is unscoped and was not confirmed for either reviewed engine/year branch.

sourceEvidence.title: Timing Belt Failure - Critical on Turbo Models
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace timing belt, water pump, tensioner, and idler pulleys as a complete kit. Gates PowerGrip Timing Belt Kit with water pump TCKWP265C (2003-2009) or TCKWP265B (2001-2002). Mopar water pump 4694307AB. Labor is 6-8 hours due to tight engine bay. NEVER skip on turbo models.

sourceEvidence.title: Front Suspension Control Arm and Bushing Wear
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Control arm bushing replacement alone costs $255-$306. Complete control arm replacement costs $951-$1,043. Strut and shock replacement costs $541-$632. A full front suspension rebuild including control arms, ball joints, struts, and alignment can cost $1,500-$2,500.

decisions.reason: The regulator assembly lacks side/body/application scope and Aisin RPACH-084 was not confirmed by the catalog for the frozen Sebring article.

sourceEvidence.title: Power Window Regulator and Motor Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Window regulator replacement with motor costs $227-$310 on average. Complete window regulator assemblies that include the motor are available and often recommended over repairing individual components. Labor costs are typically 1-2 hours.

decisions.reason: The article prescribes a complete aluminum oil-filter housing/oil-cooler assembly, while MAHLE GS33753 is only a gasket set and is the wrong repair role.

sourceEvidence.title: 3.6L Pentastar V6 Oil Filter Housing / Oil Cooler Assembly Cracking (Oil & Coolant Leaks)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the oil filter housing / oil cooler assembly along with the O-rings and gaskets. The commonly preferred fix is an aftermarket aluminum housing (e.g., Dorman) rather than the original plastic unit, which resists heat-related cracking and helps prevent recurrence. Coolant and oil are drained/refilled as part of the job. Torque the filter cap to spec (do not overtighten) to avoid cracking the replacement.
